Michelle Randolph opened up about the challenges that came with returning to her role as Ainsley in Landman after major filming delays.

“It’s always weird getting back into the groove of a project,” Randolph, 29, exclusively told Us at the premiere of her new Prime Video movie, Clashing Through the Snow . “You’re getting back into the rhythm of how the set works and all the dynamics and the personalities on set.”

Randolph was excited to be reacquainted with Ainsley , adding, “I feel like I’ve almost grown up with [Ainsley] at [this] point, because I was 24 when I booked the show. She’s my better half. I wish I looked at life like she does.”

Based on the “Boomtown” podcast, Landman is part of the Taylor Sheridan TV universe alongside Yellowstone, Mayor of Kingstown, Tulsa King, Lawmen: Bass Reeves and Lioness . The hit Paramount+ series introduced Billy Bob Thornton as a corporate fixer working for an oil titan in a West Texas-set drama with life-and-death stakes.

When Is 'Landman' Returning for Season 3? Filming Updates Explained 

Landman began filming in Texas in early 2024 , premiering its first season that November. Production on season 2 started in April 2025 and ended that August, with the episodes airing in November 2025.

While season 3 was originally scheduled to film in May, it was pushed three months later. Production was delayed again before filming finally began in October. Randolph was seen in character at Texas Christian University earlier this month.

items.title: New Bachelor Sam Hartman Admits He's Never Watched the Show

NFL quarterback Sam Hartman has a lot to learn before starting his Bachelor journey.

“I haven’t seen an episode,” the 27-year-old athlete admitted to reporters on Thursday, November 19. “So if you guys have any tips, I would love to hear your thoughts on the dos and do nots.”

Hartman added, “I’m gonna probably do some tape watching after the season’s over and study up.”

The Washington Commanders player was announced as the season 30 Bachelor earlier this month and has maintained that he’ll be able to balance his football responsibilities with filming reality TV .

Everything to Know So Far About Sam Hartman's 'The Bachelor' Season

“It’s a really, really, really interesting assessment of not only where our world is, but where Hollywood is as well,” Lowe said on the podcast. “So, I read the script. It was written by Ben Shapiro. I called Ben and said, ‘This is fantastic.’”

Lowe continued, “And he goes, ‘You’re good with it?’ I said, ‘I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world. Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’”

They didn’t have much time to talk until the end of their shifts when he came to apologize. Things took a turn, however, when Wes collapsed because his legs stopped working and he said he could no longer feel them.

This surprise story line comes after Wes revealed he had CVID (common variable immunodeficiency) and the condition prevented him from being able to get vaccinated. He was placed on leave after coming in contact with a patient with measles and wasn’t able to return to the hospital for 28 days while they waited to see if he would develop symptoms.

Simeone, meanwhile, had a difficult season as well after thinking she was pregnant. She chose to terminate her pregnancy, but there were complications, so Simone had to go through a dilation and curettage (D&C), a procedure where the cervix is dilated in order to remove tissue from inside the uterus. (The procedure is commonly used for abortions and to treat missed or incomplete miscarriages.)
